title: Tanzanian Tamarind Drink
community: Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania — the cooling coastal drink
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Sherbet ya Ukwaju — chilled tamarind water sweetened with sugar, lightly spiced with ginger and cardamom, and garnished with fresh mint. Zanzibar's most refreshing drink — the sweet-sour-spiced cooling beverage that accompanies every street food meal.
longDesc: Tamarind drink is the beverage of the Zanzibar street food scene — sour, sweet, slightly spiced, and deeply refreshing in the coastal heat. It is the essential companion to urojo, mishkaki, and bhajia at the Forodhani Gardens.
steps: Dissolve tamarind paste in 1 cup warm water.
Strain through a sieve if using block tamarind.
Add remaining cold water, sugar, ginger, and cardamom.
Serve over ice with fresh mint.
chefTips: The sweet-sour balance is personal — start with less sugar and add.
Fresh ginger grated instead of ground is more vibrant.
commonMistakes: Over-sweetening — tamarind's sourness should be present.
cookingScience: Tamarind contains tartaric acid — one of the strongest natural food acids. At the concentrations used in sherbet, it stimulates salivation more effectively than other sour agents, creating the refreshing sensation characteristic of tamarind drinks.
healthBenefits: Tamarind provides iron and B vitamins.
culturalNote: Tamarind drink is the flavour of Zanzibar's evenings — sipped at the Forodhani Gardens as the sun sets over the Indian Ocean, it is one of the island's most evocative sensory experiences.
